summary: The bounding box burned into a face alert's snapshot said the raw model class 'Face' even on a recognized person, while the notification row right next to the picture named them - and the picture is the copy that actually leaves the appliance: the notification image, the AI Log zoom lightbox, 'Download with box', and every outbound destination (webhook, MQTT, Telegram, email). A new `faceBoxLabel` in `apps/mymatasan/services/notification.go` makes `alertBoxLabel` return the person exactly as enrolled - not title-cased, since that turns a name like 'van der Berg' into 'Van Der Berg' - or the fixed label 'Unknown face' for a stranger, on every face alert. In the multi-box (crowd-style) annotation path the identity is applied only when there is exactly one box, since a `MetaBox` carries a class label and confidence but never a person, and stamping one name across several boxes would misattribute the others. The AI Log's client-side detail overlay (`AlertDetailModal` in vision.js) drew the same class-name label with the identical bug and now mirrors the fix, with a new `.alert-modal-bb-label.is-identity` style that drops the class-name capitalization for a person's name. New i18n key `vi.unknownFace` added to en/ms/zh/ar for the client-side label.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema, config, or API change, and no new toggle. Every alert already carrying the `recognized` metadata key (i.e. every face alert since face recognition shipped) now draws its box with the identity instead of the class name; non-face alerts are byte-for-byte unaffected. An existing integration that parses the box label text out of the delivered image itself (rather than the structured `person`/`recognized` fields already sent alongside it) would see the text change from 'Face'/'Face NN%' to a name or 'Unknown face'.
